claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to start by asking about your child or children.

**First question: How old is your child?** (Or if you have multiple children, let's start with the first one)

The age category matters because:
- Children **under 16** automatically qualify (subject to other conditions)
- Children **aged 16-19** may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children **aged 20 or over** do not qualify for Child Benefit

Please tell me:
1. How many children do you want to check eligibility for?
2. What is the age of your child (or each child)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son, Alex. He's 19 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're looking to claim Child Benefit for your son Alex, who is 19 years old and lives with you at home.

Since Alex is 19, he falls into the 16-19 age category. This means he may still qualify for Child Benefit if he meets certain education or training requirements.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to understand Alex's education or training status. For 16-19 year olds, Child Benefit can continue if they're in approved education or training, or in some cases, for a short period after they've left education.

**Which of the following applies to Alex?**

1. **He is currently in education or training** (enrolled in an approved course)
2. **He recently left education or training** (within the last few months)
3. **Neither** - he's not in education/training and hasn't been recently

Please let me know which situation applies to Alex.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's currently in education - he's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since Alex is currently studying for his A-levels at sixth form college, he may still qualify. Now I need to check if his course meets the requirements.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! A-levels are an approved qualification for Child Benefit purposes. Now I need to check a few more details about Alex's course:

**Questions about Alex's A-level course:**

1. **Is his course full-time?** (Does it involve at least 12 hours per week of supervised study?)

2. **Is this course funded by an employer or linked to a guaranteed future job with an employer?**

3. **Is Alex married or in a civil partnership?** (This only matters if he is - if so, we'd need to check if he's financially dependent on you)

Please let me know the answers to these questions.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, it's a full-time course - he's there during the week like any normal sixth form student. 

No, it's not funded by an employer or anything like that - it's just regular sixth form.

And no, he's not married.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Alex's A-level course meets all the education requirements:
- ✓ A-levels are an approved (non-advanced) qualification
- ✓ It's full-time (12+ hours per week of supervised study)
- ✓ It's not employer-funded
- ✓ He's not married (so no dependency considerations needed)

Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check about Alex's work situation.

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week** (or not in paid work at all)?

This matters because children aged 16+ who work 24 hours or more per week are not eligible for Child Benefit, even if they're in education.

Does Alex work less than 24 hours per week (including if he doesn't work at all)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, he does work - he has a part-time job at the local supermarket. He works quite a bit to save up for university, so it's more than 24 hours a week. But he's still doing his A-levels full-time as well.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see - so Alex is working more than 24 hours per week at the supermarket while also studying full-time for his A-levels. That's quite a demanding schedule!

Unfortunately, this does affect his eligibility. Let me navigate to the outcome for this situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that based on the information provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Why Alex is ineligible:**

Even though Alex is studying full-time for his A-levels (which is approved education), the rules state that children aged 16 or over who work **24 or more hours per week** do not qualify for Child Benefit.

**Important information:**

- Child Benefit stops when a 16-19 year old starts working 24+ hours per week, even if they're still in full-time education
- This rule applies regardless of whether the work is part-time alongside studies

**What happens next:**

- If Alex reduces his working hours to **less than 24 hours per week** while continuing his A-levels, you could become eligible to claim Child Benefit again
- Once he finishes his A-levels and goes to university (if he does), he would no longer qualify anyway as university degrees are considered "advanced education"

**Would you like any clarification** about this decision or information about what might change your eligibility in the future?
